findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Character.lean:64 `theorem char_one`, :90/:185 `char_conj`, :94/:189 `char_dual`, :134/:233 `char_orthonormal` — all abbreviate to `char`. Rubric: consistency with adjacent declarations.
findings.fix: Rename to the `char` prefix to match adjacent API: `isIntegral_char`, `char_mem_adjoin_of_isPrimitiveRoot`, `exists_multiset_char_eq_sum`(`_of_splits`), `norm_char_le_finrank`.
findings.issue: New lemmas in the `Representation`/`FDRep` namespaces name the character `character`, but every existing Mathlib lemma in those exact namespaces uses the abbreviation `char` (`char_one`, `char_conj`, `char_dual`, `char_tensor`, `char_orthonormal`). Affected: `exists_multiset_character_eq_sum_of_splits`, `exists_multiset_character_eq_sum`, `isIntegral_character_of_splits`, `isIntegral_character`, `character_mem_adjoin_of_isPrimitiveRoot`, `norm_character_apply_le_finrank` (both `Representation.*` and `FDRep.*`).

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Character.lean:90 `char_conj` states `ρ.character g` with no `_apply`; no `character_apply`/`char_apply` lemma exists in Mathlib.
findings.fix: Drop `_apply`: `norm_char_le_finrank` (consistent with the char-prefix fix above).
findings.issue: `norm_character_apply_le_finrank` adds an `_apply` suffix for `ρ.character g`, but Mathlib's character-value lemmas name the value at a point without `_apply` (e.g. `char_conj (g : G) : ... ρ.character g`), and the PR's own sibling `isIntegral_character` omits it — inconsistent and gratuitous.

summary: The new character-value lemmas use the full word `character` in their names, breaking consistency with Mathlib's existing `char_`-prefixed API (`char_one`, `char_conj`, `char_dual`, ...) in the same `Representation`/`FDRep` namespaces. One lemma also carries a gratuitous `_apply`.
